cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Sound in film is divided into diegetic, originating from within the film world, and non-diegetic, added for the audience from outside the narrative world.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Diegetic sound includes dialogue, ambient sound, on-screen music and sound effects that characters can theoretically hear.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Non-diegetic sound includes the musical score, voice-over narration and sound effects added for dramatic effect that characters cannot hear.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Sound can be further divided into on-screen and off-screen, with off-screen sound extending the diegetic world beyond the visible frame.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Parallel sound matches the mood or tone of the image, reinforcing the emotional content — e.g. tense music during a suspenseful scene.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Contrapuntal sound deliberately contrasts with the image, creating irony, unease or prompting the audience to read the scene differently.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Silence is a powerful sound design choice that can create tension, intimacy, shock or contemplation by removing expected audio information.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: A sound bridge carries audio from one scene into the next, creating continuity and linking scenes through shared aural information.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Foley is the reproduction of everyday sound effects added in post-production to enhance the audio quality and realism of a film's soundtrack.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: The musical score contributes significantly to emotional manipulation of the audience, with tempo, instrumentation and volume all affecting mood.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Sound motifs are recurring sounds or musical phrases associated with a particular character, location or theme, gaining meaning through repetition.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sound in Film
cards.back: Analysis of sound must consider how it interacts with other film language elements such as editing, cinematography and mise-en-scene.
